newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Minnow Cairn links with Shell in Asia.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Minnow Cairn links with Shell in Asia.

text.p: Cairn Energy Plc rose by 1.4 percent on Tuesday after the British oil minnow said it is to form an alliance with giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group to develop interests in Bangladesh and part of India.
The deal highlights the attraction of Cairn's massive gas discovery offshore Bangladesh and marks Shell's third effort to become active in the country, analysts said.
The Anglo-Dutch mammoth tried and failed twice in the past three decades to start commercially viable operations in Bangladesh, but is entering again after Cairn discovered the Sangu field last year.
Under the terms of the alliance, Shell will pay Cairn $130 million and fund the first $200 million of any new successful exploration programme, Cairn said.
In return, Shell will receive 25 percent of Cairn's Bangladeshi interests and another quarter if Cairn and Shell are successful in another round of bidding for new acreage in Bangladesh.
The Sangu field, in which Cairn has a 75 percent interest, is estimated to have proved and probable reserves of more than 800 billion cubic feet. Production is to set to start in April 1998
The Shell-Cairn alliance suggests Shell is no longer sticking to a policy of doing everything on its own, while strongly enhancing Cairn's financial position, industry watchers said.
"It (the alliance) gives them the opportunity to expand elsewhere or make any acquisitions," said analyst Peter Hitchens at broker Willams de Broe.

Cairn, meanwhile, sang the praises of Shell, saying the Anglo-Dutch company was its preferred candidate because of Shell's strong presence in Asia and dismissed fears the alliance would make Cairn a less attractive takeover candidate.
Analysts had feared the deal might leave Shell with pre-emptive rights to buy Cairn's attractive assets if a bid for the company is launched by a third party.
But Cairn chief operating officer Malcolm Thoms told Reuters, "There are no poisons or pills in this deal."
Fuelled by Sangu's potential and hopes of a takeover, Cairn's shares have been among the best-performing on the London stock exchange. They have gained a total 423 percent since the start of 1996.
On Tuesday, Cairn closed 8-1/2 pence higher at 594-1/2, while Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc -- the British arm of the Shell Group -- firmed 9-1/2 to 1,077.
